 462: def open_round(
 463:     packet_analysis_run_id: str,
 464:     *,
 465:     packet,  # noqa: ANN001 - CasePacket, imported lazily to avoid a cycle
 466:     bundle_id: str,
 467:     available_evidence: frozenset[str] = TYPICAL_AVAILABLE_EVIDENCE,
 468: ) -> AnalysisRequest:
 469:     """Open a round against the shipped catalog. Convenience for integration."""
 470:     return AnalysisRequest(
 471:         analysis_run_id=packet_analysis_run_id,
 472:         analyst_bundle_id=bundle_id,
 473:         packet=packet,
 474:         catalog=TOOL_CATALOG,
 475:         available_evidence=available_evidence,
 476:     )

1: """The wire between the platform and an external analyst â€” E5.
   2: 
   3: Everything an untrusted analyst can do to this system passes through the
   4: three objects here: it is handed an :class:`AnalysisRequest`, it sends
   5: :class:`ToolRequest` messages, and it receives :class:`ToolResult`
   6: messages. It returns an :class:`AnalysisResponse` of hypotheses. There is
   7: no fourth channel, and in particular there is no channel on which a
   8: model can hand over a finding.
   9: 
  10: **The analyst cannot manufacture evidence, by shape.** A
  11: :class:`HypothesisProposal` has no status, no confidence and no
  12: measurement â€” E0 took those fields away. A :class:`ToolResult` has all
  13: of them, and the only way one comes into existence is
  14: :meth:`ToolSession.record` against a request the same session admitted.
  15: An analyst that fabricates a result is holding an object nothing will
  16: accept: the session has no admitted request with that id, so the result
  17: never becomes a :class:`~planbench_explanation.ledger.CheckerResult` and
  18: never reaches the promotion matrix.
  19: 
  20: That is the substance behind "only the tool host may sign a result".
  21: A cryptographic signature would prove the same thing to a third party
  22: across a trust boundary; within one process the binding to an admitted
  23: request is what actually holds, so that is what is implemented rather
  24: than a signature field an analyst could also fill in.
  25: 
  26: **Admission is where the catalog stops being documentation.** Every
  27: request is checked against the card: does the tool exist at that
  28: version, is it on the menu this analysis was opened with, is the run and
  29: the packet and the bundle the one being analysed, does the evidence the
  30: card requires actually exist for this run, and is the tool allowed to
  31: execute at all. Research-proposal tools fail that last check by
  32: construction â€” they write specifications, and a specification is not a
  33: run.
  34: 
  35: **Two words that must never merge.** ``execution_status`` says how the
  36: tool ran; ``proposition_verdict`` says whether the proposition stood.
  37: A single ``pass`` covering both is how "the checker ran fine and refuted
  38: the hypothesis" turns into "the check passed". They are separate fields
  39: with separate vocabularies and a validator between them: a tool that did
  40: not complete has no verdict at all.
  41: 
  42: **A top-level verdict belongs only to a single-proposition tool.** A
  43: tool answering about three propositions and reporting one verdict is
  44: reporting an aggregate nobody defined â€” so multi-proposition results
  45: carry their verdicts inside the entries and leave the top level empty.
  46: 
  47: **The host stamps the over-readings.** ``unsupported_inferences`` is not
  48: something a checker chooses per run; it is the card's
  49: ``forbidden_inference_types``, copied onto every result so the refusal
  50: travels with the evidence. A result that dropped one would be a result
  51: that quietly permits the reading its card forbids, and the drop would be
  52: invisible at the far end.
  53: 
  54: **The shape of the data is closed too, not only the conclusions.**
  55: Arguments are checked against the card's :class:`~planbench_explanation.tools.ToolIO`
  56: at admission; measurements and references at recording. Without that,
  57: the catalog locks which tool may say what while leaving every checker
  58: free to invent its own argument names â€” and by the time four of them
  59: exist, the contract is whatever the first one did.
  60: 
  61: Both halves of the output are closed, and for a while only one was.
  62: Barring unknown measurement keys stops a checker inventing ``width``,
  63: but a completed result carrying **no** measurements at all was still
  64: well formed â€” a check that reports nothing is not a check that found
  65: nothing. And a navigation tool reporting ``n_exemplars: 4`` had told the
  66: caller how many episodes to open without saying which, because every
  67: output was being squeezed through a mapping of floats. Pointers are now
  68: :class:`EvidenceReference` values with a typed kind, and a card that
  69: declares one requires it.
  70: 
  71: **A request is about a hypothesis the analyst actually declared, and
  72: declaring is by content.** The session is told the proposals first; a
  73: request naming a hypothesis id nobody proposed is refused. Otherwise
  74: ``hypothesis_id`` is a free-text field, the round cannot be
  75: reconstructed as a line of reasoning, and evidence gathered "for" a
  76: hypothesis that never existed still lands in the ledger.
  77: 
  78: Registering ids alone would leave the interesting half open: re-declare
  79: ``hyp-004`` mid-round with a different proposition and subject, and the
  80: evidence gathered for the first hypothesis silently becomes evidence for
  81: the second. So the session keeps a checksum per id â€” re-declaring the
  82: same content is idempotent, re-declaring different content under one id
  83: is refused, and an ``AnalysisResponse`` from another round or another
  84: bundle is refused before any of it is registered. A refused declaration
  85: registers **nothing**: the whole batch is checked before any of it is
  86: written, so a caller that catches the rejection and a session that
  87: raised it still agree on what was declared.
  88: 
  89: **Failure codes are a closed union.** Each card enumerates its own
  90: failure modes; the host contributes the generic ones in
  91: :data:`HOST_FAILURE_CODES`. A code outside the union is refused, because
  92: a failure nobody enumerated is a failure nobody designed for â€” and the
  93: downstream reader cannot tell it from a typo.
  94: """
  95: 
  96: from __future__ import annotations
  97: 
  98: from collections.abc import Iterable, Sequence
  99: from typing import Any, Literal
 100: 
 101: from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, model_validator
 102: 
 103: from planbench_explanation.case_packet import CasePacket
 104: from planbench_explanation.ledger import (
 105:     CheckerResult,
 106:     HypothesisProposal,
 107:     PropositionOutcome,
 108: )
 109: from planbench_explanation.propositions import PropositionType
 110: from planbench_explanation.provenance import (
 111:     ExecutionStatus,
 112:     InputProvenance,
 113:     PropositionVerdict,
 114: )
 115: from planbench_explanation.tools import ToolCard, ToolCatalog, ToolNotInCatalog
 116: from planbench_explanation.versioning import (
 117:     CHECKSUM_PATTERN,
 118:     CODE_REF_PATTERN,
 119:     artifact_checksum,
 120: )
 121: 
 122: #: Why a request or a result was turned away. A closed vocabulary so a
 123: #: harness can count rejections by kind rather than by matching prose.
 124: RejectionCode = Literal[
 125:     "unknown_tool",
 126:     "catalog_version_mismatch",
 127:     "packet_mismatch",
 128:     "analysis_run_mismatch",
 129:     "bundle_mismatch",
 130:     "duplicate_request_id",
 131:     "sequence_out_of_order",
 132:     "request_budget_exhausted",
 133:     "missing_required_evidence",
 134:     "execution_not_authorized",
 135:     "unknown_hypothesis",
 136:     "unknown_request",
 137:     "duplicate_result",
 138:     "tool_mismatch",
 139:     "provenance_not_allowed",
 140:     "proposition_not_supported",
 141:     "inference_refusal_dropped",
 142:     "arguments_rejected",
 143:     "measurements_rejected",
 144:     "references_rejected",
 145:     "unknown_failure_code",
 146:     "hypothesis_redefined",
 147: ]
 148: 
 149: 
 150: #: Failures that belong to the host rather than to any tool. Kept
 151: #: apart from a card's ``failure_modes`` because a card should not have
 152: #: to enumerate the ways the platform itself can break, and because a
 153: #: reader wants to know which side failed.
 154: HOST_FAILURE_CODES: tuple[str, ...] = (
 155:     "checker_not_implemented",
 156:     "checker_timeout",
 157:     "host_internal_error",
 158:     "tool_unavailable",
 159: )
 160: 
 161: 
 162: class ProtocolRejection(ValueError):
 163:     """A message the host refuses to process, with a machine-readable code."""
 164: 
 165:     def __init__(self, code: RejectionCode, message: str) -> None:
 166:         self.code: RejectionCode = code
 167:         super().__init__(f"{code}: {message}")

 170: class AnalysisRequest(BaseModel):
 171:     """What the platform opens an analysis round with.
 172: 
 173:     The packet is the analyst's whole view of the case (E4); the catalog
 174:     is its whole vocabulary of actions. ``available_evidence`` is the
 175:     third thing it needs and the one most easily forgotten: which kinds
 176:     of evidence this particular run actually holds. A run recorded
 177:     before the trace address changed has no per-episode trace, and an
 178:     analyst that asks for one should be told so at admission rather than
 179:     handed an empty result to interpret.
 180:     """
 181: 
 182:     model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")
 183: 
 184:     analysis_run_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
 185:     analyst_bundle_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
 186:     packet: CasePacket
 187:     catalog: ToolCatalog
 188:     #: Evidence keys this run holds, matched against each card's
 189:     #: ``required_evidence``. Declared by the platform, never by the
 190:     #: analyst.
 191:     available_evidence: frozenset[str] = frozenset()
 192:     #: Ceiling on tool requests in one round. A round is a budget, and a
 193:     #: budget nobody enforces is a suggestion.
 194:     max_tool_requests: int = Field(default=64, ge=1, le=1024)
 195: 
 196:     @property
 197:     def case_packet_checksum(self) -> str:
 198:         return artifact_checksum(self.packet.model_dump(mode="json"))
 199:

 201: class ToolRequest(BaseModel):
 202:     """One action an analyst asks the host to take.
 203: 
 204:     Every identity field is here so a request can be placed later:
 205:     which round, which packet, which menu, which analyst build, and
 206:     where in the sequence. A request that names none of these is a
 207:     request nobody can attribute after the fact.
 208:     """
 209: 
 210:     model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")
 211: 
 212:     #: Bounded and printable. It is an analyst-supplied string that ends
 213:     #: up in filenames and log lines, and the file sink hashes it before
 214:     #: using it as a path â€” but a value that cannot be a path in the
 215:     #: first place is one fewer thing to reason about.
 216:     request_id: str = Field(min_length=1, max_length=128, pattern=r"^[A-Za-z0-9_.:-]+$")
 217:     analysis_run_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
 218:     case_packet_checksum: str = Field(pattern=CHECKSUM_PATTERN)
 219:     tool_catalog_version: str = Field(min_length=1)
 220:     analyst_bundle_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
 221:     sequence: int = Field(ge=1)
 222:     tool_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
 223:     tool_version: str = Field(min_length=1)
 224:     hypothesis_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
 225:     arguments: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
 226:     evidence_refs: tuple[str, ...] = ()
 227: 
 228: 
 229: class EvidenceReference(BaseModel):
 230:     """A pointer a navigation tool returns: what kind, and which one.
 231: 
 232:     Separate from ``measurements`` because it is not a number, and a
 233:     count of pointers is not a pointer. ``ref`` is opaque here â€” its
 234:     grammar belongs to the kind â€” but it is the string a viewer resolves,
 235:     so it may not be blank.
 236:     """
 237: 
 238:     model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")
 239: 
 240:     kind: str = Field(min_length=1)
 241:     ref: str = Field(min_length=1)
 242:     label: str | None = None
 243: 
 244: 
 245: class ToolResult(BaseModel):
 246:     """What the host returns. Never constructed by an analyst.
 247: 
 248:     Well-formedness is enforced here; whether the result *belongs* to an
 249:     admitted request is enforced by :meth:`ToolSession.record`, because
 250:     that is a fact about the session and not about the message.
 251:     """
 252: 
 253:     model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid", allow_inf_nan=False)
 254: 
 255:     request_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
 256:     tool_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
 257:     tool_version: str = Field(min_length=1)
 258:     execution_status: ExecutionStatus
 259:     input_provenance: InputProvenance
 260:     proposition_verdict: PropositionVerdict | None = None
 261:     supported_propositions: tuple[PropositionOutcome, ...] = ()
 262:     unsupported_inferences: tuple[PropositionType, ...] = ()
 263:     measurements: dict[str, float] = Field(default_factory=dict)
 264:     #: Typed pointers into the evidence. Empty for tools that compute
 265:     #: rather than locate; required for the ones whose whole job is to
 266:     #: say where to look.
 267:     references: tuple[EvidenceReference, ...] = ()
 268:     failure_code: str | None = None
 269:     evidence_artifact_ref: str | None = None
 270:     evidence_checksum: str | None = Field(default=None, pattern=CHECKSUM_PATTERN)
 271:     implementation_ref: str | None = Field(default=None, pattern=CODE_REF_PATTERN)
 272: 
 273:     @model_validator(mode="after")
 274:     def _check(self) -> ToolResult:
 275:         if self.execution_status != "completed":
 276:             if self.proposition_verdict is not None:
 277:                 raise ProtocolRejection(
 278:                     "tool_mismatch",
 279:                     f"execution_status={self.execution_status!r} carries "
 280:                     f"proposition_verdict={self.proposition_verdict!r}. A tool that did "
 281:                     "not complete has not adjudicated anything; how it ran and whether "
 282:                     "the proposition stood are different questions.",
 283:                 )
 284:             if self.supported_propositions:
 285:                 raise ProtocolRejection(
 286:                     "tool_mismatch",
 287:                     f"execution_status={self.execution_status!r} lists propositions; a "
 288:                     "run that did not complete produced no outcomes",
 289:                 )
 290:             if self.failure_code is None:
 291:                 raise ProtocolRejection(
 292:                     "tool_mismatch",
 293:                     f"execution_status={self.execution_status!r} with no failure_code; "
 294:                     "the card enumerates its failure modes so a reader can tell "
 295:                     "'no inputs' from 'the checker crashed'",
 296:                 )
 297:             return self
 298: 
 299:         missing = [
 300:             name
 301:             for name, value in (
 302:                 ("evidence_artifact_ref", self.evidence_artifact_ref),
 303:                 ("evidence_checksum", self.evidence_checksum),
 304:                 ("implementation_ref", self.implementation_ref),
 305:             )
 306:             if value is None
 307:         ]
 308:         if missing:
 309:             raise ProtocolRejection(
 310:                 "tool_mismatch",
 311:                 f"a completed result is missing {missing}; a verdict nobody can trace "
 312:                 "back to an artifact and a build is a verdict on trust",
 313:             )
 314:         if self.failure_code is not None:
 315:             raise ProtocolRejection(
 316:                 "tool_mismatch",
 317:                 f"a completed result carries failure_code={self.failure_code!r}",
 318:             )
 319:         if not self.supported_propositions:
 320:             if self.proposition_verdict is not None:
 321:                 raise ProtocolRejection(
 322:                     "tool_mismatch",
 323:                     "a top-level verdict with no proposition behind it says a "
 324:                     "something stood without saying what",
 325:                 )
 326:             return self
 327:         if len(self.supported_propositions) == 1:
 328:             if self.proposition_verdict is None:
 329:                 raise ProtocolRejection(
 330:                     "tool_mismatch",
 331:                     "a single-proposition result must state its verdict at the top "
 332:                     "level, where the promotion matrix reads it",
 333:                 )
 334:             if self.proposition_verdict != self.supported_propositions[0].result:
 335:                 raise ProtocolRejection(
 336:                     "tool_mismatch",
 337:                     f"top-level verdict {self.proposition_verdict!r} disagrees with the "
 338:                     f"one proposition's {self.supported_propositions[0].result!r}",
 339:                 )
 340:         elif self.proposition_verdict is not None:
 341:             raise ProtocolRejection(
 342:                 "tool_mismatch",
 343:                 "a multi-proposition result has no single verdict; an aggregate over "
 344:                 "several propositions is a number nobody defined. Leave the top level "
 345:                 "empty and let each entry carry its own.",
 346:             )
 347:         return self
 348: 
 349:     def as_checker_result(self) -> CheckerResult:
 350:         """The same facts in the ledger's vocabulary."""
 351:         return CheckerResult(
 352:             request_id=self.request_id,
 353:             tool_id=self.tool_id,
 354:             tool_version=self.tool_version,
 355:             execution_status=self.execution_status,
 356:             input_provenance=self.input_provenance,
 357:             proposition_verdict=self.proposition_verdict,
 358:             supported_propositions=self.supported_propositions,
 359:             unsupported_inferences=self.unsupported_inferences,
 360:             measurements=self.measurements,
 361:             evidence_artifact_ref=self.evidence_artifact_ref,
 362:             evidence_checksum=self.evidence_checksum,
 363:             implementation_ref=self.implementation_ref,
 364:         )

 367: class AnalysisResponse(BaseModel):
 368:     """What the analyst hands back at the end of a round.
 369: 
 370:     Abstention is a first-class answer with its own field rather than an
 371:     empty proposal list, because "I found nothing worth proposing" and
 372:     "I crashed" produce the same empty list and must not be scored the
 373:     same way.
 374:     """
 375: 
 376:     model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")
 377: 
 378:     analysis_run_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
 379:     analyst_bundle_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
 380:     proposals: tuple[HypothesisProposal, ...] = ()
 381:     abstained: bool = False
 382:     abstention_reason: str | None = None
 383: 
 384:     @model_validator(mode="after")
 385:     def _check(self) -> AnalysisResponse:
 386:         if self.abstained and self.proposals:
 387:             raise ProtocolRejection(
 388:                 "tool_mismatch",
 389:                 "an abstention with proposals attached is not an abstention; say "
 390:                 "nothing or say something",
 391:             )
 392:         if self.abstained and not self.abstention_reason:
 393:             raise ProtocolRejection(
 394:                 "tool_mismatch",
 395:                 "an abstention with no reason cannot be told from a silent failure",
 396:             )
 397:         ids = [proposal.hypothesis_id for proposal in self.proposals]
 398:         duplicates = sorted({item for item in ids if ids.count(item) > 1})
 399:         if duplicates:
 400:             raise ProtocolRejection(
 401:                 "tool_mismatch", f"hypothesis id(s) {duplicates} proposed twice"
 402:             )
 403:         return self

 406: class ToolSession:
 407:     """The host side of one analysis round.
 408: 
 409:     Stateful on purpose. Admission needs to know what has already been
 410:     asked â€” the sequence so far, which request ids are spent, how much of
 411:     the budget is left â€” and a stateless check cannot see any of that.
 412:     """
 413: 
 414:     def __init__(self, analysis: AnalysisRequest) -> None:
 415:         self.analysis = analysis
 416:         self._checksum = analysis.case_packet_checksum
 417:         self._admitted: dict[str, tuple[ToolRequest, ToolCard]] = {}
 418:         self._answered: set[str] = set()
 419:         self._results: dict[str, ToolResult] = {}
 420:         self._hypotheses: dict[str, str] = {}
 421:         self._last_sequence = 0
 422: 
 423:     @property
 424:     def declared_hypotheses(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
 425:         return tuple(sorted(self._hypotheses))
 426: 
 427:     def declare(self, proposals: Iterable[HypothesisProposal] | AnalysisResponse) -> None:
 428:         """Register the hypotheses this round may gather evidence for.
 429: 
 430:         Callable more than once: a real analyst proposes, checks, and
 431:         proposes again in light of what came back, and a contract that
 432:         allowed only one declaration would force it to guess its whole
 433:         line of reasoning before seeing any evidence.
 434: 
 435:         What it may not do is reuse an id. Each is bound to the checksum
 436:         of the proposal it was declared with, so declaring the same
 437:         proposal twice is a no-op and declaring a different one under
 438:         the same id is refused â€” otherwise evidence gathered for one
 439:         hypothesis becomes evidence for another by renaming.
 440:         """
 441:         if isinstance(proposals, AnalysisResponse):
 442:             if proposals.analysis_run_id != self.analysis.analysis_run_id:
 443:                 raise ProtocolRejection(
 444:                     "analysis_run_mismatch",
 445:                     f"response is from round {proposals.analysis_run_id!r}, this "
 446:                     f"session is {self.analysis.analysis_run_id!r}",
 447:                 )
 448:             if proposals.analyst_bundle_id != self.analysis.analyst_bundle_id:
 449:                 raise ProtocolRejection(
 450:                     "bundle_mismatch",
 451:                     f"response is from bundle {proposals.analyst_bundle_id!r}, this "
 452:                     f"round was opened for {self.analysis.analyst_bundle_id!r}",
 453:                 )
 454:             proposals = proposals.proposals
 455: 
 456:         # Check the whole batch before writing any of it. Checking and
 457:         # writing in one pass meant a batch refused on its third
 458:         # proposal had already registered the first two: the caller sees
 459:         # an exception, the session has changed, and neither of them
 460:         # agrees with the other about what was declared.
 461:         staged: dict[str, str] = {}
 462:         for proposal in proposals:
 463:             checksum = artifact_checksum(proposal.model_dump(mode="json"))
 464:             known = self._hypotheses.get(proposal.hypothesis_id) or staged.get(
 465:                 proposal.hypothesis_id
 466:             )
 467:             if known is not None and known != checksum:
 468:                 raise ProtocolRejection(
 469:                     "hypothesis_redefined",
 470:                     f"{proposal.hypothesis_id!r} was already declared with different "
 471:                     "content. Reusing an id would move the evidence already gathered "
 472:                     "under it onto a different claim; give the new hypothesis its own id.",
 473:                 )
 474:             staged[proposal.hypothesis_id] = checksum
 475:         self._hypotheses.update(staged)
 476: 
 477:     def proposal_checksum(self, hypothesis_id: str) -> str:
 478:         """What was declared under this id. For an auditor rebuilding a round."""
 479:         try:
 480:             return self._hypotheses[hypothesis_id]
 481:         except KeyError as error:
 482:             raise ProtocolRejection(
 483:                 "unknown_hypothesis", f"no proposal {hypothesis_id!r} in this round"
 484:             ) from error
 485: 
 486:     @property
 487:     def admitted(self) -> tuple[ToolRequest, ...]:
 488:         return tuple(request for request, _ in self._admitted.values())
 489: 
 490:     @property
 491:     def requested_tool_ids(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
 492:         """Which tools were asked for, in order. What golden scores."""
 493:         return tuple(request.tool_id for request, _ in self._admitted.values())
 494: 
 495:     def admit(self, request: ToolRequest) -> ToolCard:
 496:         """Accept a request, or refuse it with a coded reason."""
 497:         analysis = self.analysis
 498:         if request.analysis_run_id != analysis.analysis_run_id:
 499:             raise ProtocolRejection(
 500:                 "analysis_run_mismatch",
 501:                 f"request names round {request.analysis_run_id!r}, this session is "
 502:                 f"{analysis.analysis_run_id!r}",
 503:             )
 504:         if request.analyst_bundle_id != analysis.analyst_bundle_id:
 505:             raise ProtocolRejection(
 506:                 "bundle_mismatch",
 507:                 f"request names bundle {request.analyst_bundle_id!r}, this round was "
 508:                 f"opened for {analysis.analyst_bundle_id!r}. A round is attributable to "
 509:                 "one frozen analyst or to none.",
 510:             )
 511:         if request.case_packet_checksum != self._checksum:
 512:             raise ProtocolRejection(
 513:                 "packet_mismatch",
 514:                 "request answers a different case packet than this round was opened with",
 515:             )
 516:         if request.tool_catalog_version != analysis.catalog.catalog_version:
 517:             raise ProtocolRejection(
 518:                 "catalog_version_mismatch",
 519:                 f"request chose from menu {request.tool_catalog_version!r}, this round "
 520:                 f"serves {analysis.catalog.catalog_version!r}",
 521:             )
 522:         if request.request_id in self._admitted:
 523:             raise ProtocolRejection(
 524:                 "duplicate_request_id",
 525:                 f"request id {request.request_id!r} was already admitted; ids are how "
 526:                 "results are matched to requests",
 527:             )
 528:         if request.sequence <= self._last_sequence:
 529:             raise ProtocolRejection(
 530:                 "sequence_out_of_order",
 531:                 f"sequence {request.sequence} follows {self._last_sequence}; the order "
 532:                 "of a round is part of what a reviewer reconstructs",
 533:             )
 534:         if len(self._admitted) >= analysis.max_tool_requests:
 535:             raise ProtocolRejection(
 536:                 "request_budget_exhausted",
 537:                 f"round budget of {analysis.max_tool_requests} tool requests is spent",
 538:             )
 539: 
 540:         if request.hypothesis_id not in self._hypotheses:
 541:             raise ProtocolRejection(
 542:                 "unknown_hypothesis",
 543:                 f"no proposal {request.hypothesis_id!r} was declared in this round; "
 544:                 "evidence is gathered for a stated hypothesis or it is gathered for "
 545:                 "nothing, and a round nobody can read as a line of reasoning is a "
 546:                 "round nobody can review",
 547:             )
 548: 
 549:         try:
 550:             card = analysis.catalog.card(request.tool_id, request.tool_version)
 551:         except ToolNotInCatalog as error:
 552:             raise ProtocolRejection("unknown_tool", str(error)) from error
 553: 
 554:         if not card.execution_authorized:
 555:             raise ProtocolRejection(
 556:                 "execution_not_authorized",
 557:                 f"{card.tool_id} writes a specification for an experiment; running one "
 558:                 "is a decision a person makes in the research lane",
 559:             )
 560:         missing = sorted(set(card.required_evidence) - analysis.available_evidence)
 561:         if missing:
 562:             raise ProtocolRejection(
 563:                 "missing_required_evidence",
 564:                 f"{card.tool_id} needs {missing}, which this run does not hold. Being "
 565:                 "told so is the answer; an empty result would be read as a finding.",
 566:             )
 567:         problems = card.io.check_arguments(request.arguments)
 568:         if problems:
 569:             raise ProtocolRejection("arguments_rejected", f"{card.tool_id}: " + "; ".join(problems))
 570: 
 571:         self._admitted[request.request_id] = (request, card)
 572:         self._last_sequence = request.sequence
 573:         return card
 574: 
 575:     def record(self, result: ToolResult) -> ToolResult:
 576:         """Bind a result to its admitted request, or refuse it.
 577: 
 578:         This is the narrow gate. A result whose request this session
 579:         never admitted has nowhere to attach, which is what stops an
 580:         analyst from writing its own evidence.
 581: 
 582:         Returns the result rather than a ledger row because **most tools
 583:         do not produce ledger rows**. A fact query hands over the Î”U
 584:         decomposition and a navigation tool hands over four episode ids;
 585:         neither adjudicates a proposition, and a
 586:         :class:`~planbench_explanation.ledger.CheckerResult` that
 587:         adjudicates nothing is a row the promotion matrix would have to
 588:         skip. Use :attr:`checker_results` for the ones that do.
 589:         """
 590:         found = self._admitted.get(result.request_id)
 591:         if found is None:
 592:             raise ProtocolRejection(
 593:                 "unknown_request",
 594:                 f"no admitted request {result.request_id!r} in this round; a result "
 595:                 "for a request the host never accepted is a result the host never "
 596:                 "produced",
 597:             )
 598:         request, card = found
 599:         if result.request_id in self._answered:
 600:             raise ProtocolRejection(
 601:                 "duplicate_result",
 602:                 f"request {result.request_id!r} already has a result; a second one "
 603:                 "would let the better of two answers be kept",
 604:             )
 605:         if (result.tool_id, result.tool_version) != (request.tool_id, request.tool_version):
 606:             raise ProtocolRejection(
 607:                 "tool_mismatch",
 608:                 f"result claims {result.tool_id}@{result.tool_version} for a request "
 609:                 f"for {request.tool_id}@{request.tool_version}",
 610:             )
 611: 
 612:         allowed = card.evidence_policy.allowed_input_provenance
 613:         if result.input_provenance not in allowed:
 614:             checkable = result.execution_status == "not_checkable"
 615:             if not (checkable and result.input_provenance == "missing"):
 616:                 raise ProtocolRejection(
 617:                     "provenance_not_allowed",
 618:                     f"{card.tool_id} accepts {list(allowed)} but the result declares "
 619:                     f"{result.input_provenance!r}",
 620:                 )
 621: 
 622:         supported = set(card.proposition_policy.supported_proposition_types)
 623:         offered = {outcome.proposition_type for outcome in result.supported_propositions}
 624:         beyond = sorted(offered - supported)
 625:         if beyond:
 626:             raise ProtocolRejection(
 627:                 "proposition_not_supported",
 628:                 f"{card.tool_id} reported on {beyond}, which its card does not support. "
 629:                 "The card is the menu of what this checker can establish, and a result "
 630:                 "outside it is a checker answering a question it was not built for.",
 631:             )
 632:         required_refusals = set(card.proposition_policy.forbidden_inference_types)
 633:         if set(result.unsupported_inferences) != required_refusals:
 634:             raise ProtocolRejection(
 635:                 "inference_refusal_dropped",
 636:                 f"{card.tool_id} forbids {sorted(required_refusals)} but the result "
 637:                 f"carries {sorted(result.unsupported_inferences)}. The refusals travel "
 638:                 "with the evidence; dropping one is how an over-reading becomes "
 639:                 "permitted downstream, silently.",
 640:             )
 641: 
 642:         completed = result.execution_status == "completed"
 643:         bad_measurements = card.io.check_measurements(result.measurements, completed=completed)
 644:         if bad_measurements:
 645:             raise ProtocolRejection("measurements_rejected", "; ".join(bad_measurements))
 646:         bad_references = card.io.check_references(
 647:             (reference.kind for reference in result.references), completed=completed
 648:         )
 649:         if bad_references:
 650:             raise ProtocolRejection("references_rejected", "; ".join(bad_references))
 651: 
 652:         if result.failure_code is not None:
 653:             allowed_codes = set(card.failure_modes) | set(HOST_FAILURE_CODES)
 654:             if result.failure_code not in allowed_codes:
 655:                 raise ProtocolRejection(
 656:                     "unknown_failure_code",
 657:                     f"{result.failure_code!r} is neither one of {card.tool_id}'s "
 658:                     f"declared failure modes {list(card.failure_modes)} nor a host "
 659:                     f"code {list(HOST_FAILURE_CODES)}; an unenumerated failure cannot "
 660:                     "be told from a typo",
 661:                 )
 662: 
 663:         self._answered.add(result.request_id)
 664:         self._results[result.request_id] = result
 665:         return result
 666: 
 667:     @property
 668:     def results(self) -> tuple[ToolResult, ...]:
 669:         """Every recorded result, in the order the requests were admitted."""
 670:         return tuple(
 671:             self._results[request_id]
 672:             for request_id in self._admitted
 673:             if request_id in self._results
 674:         )
 675: 
 676:     @property
 677:     def checker_results(self) -> tuple[CheckerResult, ...]:
 678:         """The subset that adjudicated something, in the ledger's vocabulary.
 679: 
 680:         Filtered by the *card*, not by whether a particular result
 681:         happened to come back empty: a mechanism check that failed to
 682:         run is still a checker result, and the ledger needs it to tell
 683:         "the check refuted this" from "nobody checked".
 684:         """
 685:         rows = []
 686:         for request_id, (_, card) in self._admitted.items():
 687:             if not card.proposition_policy.supported_proposition_types:
 688:                 continue
 689:             result = self._results.get(request_id)
 690:             if result is not None:
 691:                 rows.append(result.as_checker_result())
 692:         return tuple(rows)
 693: 
 694: 
 695: def stamped_result(
 696:     card: ToolCard,
 697:     request: ToolRequest,
 698:     *,
 699:     execution_status: ExecutionStatus,
 700:     input_provenance: InputProvenance,
 701:     proposition_verdict: PropositionVerdict | None = None,
 702:     supported_propositions: Sequence[PropositionOutcome] = (),
 703:     measurements: dict[str, float] | None = None,
 704:     references: Sequence[EvidenceReference] = (),
 705:     failure_code: str | None = None,
 706:     evidence_artifact_ref: str | None = None,
 707:     evidence_checksum: str | None = None,
 708:     implementation_ref: str | None = None,
 709: ) -> ToolResult:
 710:     """Build a result with the card's refusals already stamped on.
 711: 
 712:     A checker implementation should not be retyping
 713:     ``forbidden_inference_types`` â€” that is how one of them goes missing.
 714:     It comes off the card here, and :meth:`ToolSession.record` refuses
 715:     the result if it does not.
 716:     """
 717:     return ToolResult(
 718:         request_id=request.request_id,
 719:         tool_id=card.tool_id,
 720:         tool_version=card.tool_version,
 721:         execution_status=execution_status,
 722:         input_provenance=input_provenance,
 723:         proposition_verdict=proposition_verdict,
 724:         supported_propositions=tuple(supported_propositions),
 725:         unsupported_inferences=card.proposition_policy.forbidden_inference_types,
 726:         measurements=dict(measurements or {}),
 727:         references=tuple(references),
 728:         failure_code=failure_code,
 729:         evidence_artifact_ref=evidence_artifact_ref,
 730:         evidence_checksum=evidence_checksum,
 731:         implementation_ref=implementation_ref,
 732:     )

 735: def missing_evidence_for(
 736:     catalog: ToolCatalog, available: Iterable[str]
 737: ) -> dict[str, tuple[str, ...]]:
 738:     """Which tools this run cannot serve, and what each one is short of.
 739: 
 740:     Handed to an analyst alongside the packet so a round is not spent
 741:     discovering the same absence four times.
 742:     """
 743:     have = set(available)
 744:     shortfalls = {}
 745:     for card in catalog.cards:
 746:         missing = tuple(sorted(set(card.required_evidence) - have))
 747:         if missing:
 748:             shortfalls[card.tool_id] = missing
 749:     return shortfalls

1: """The tool host: admission, evidence, execution, signature â€” E6a.
   2: 
   3: E5 built the protocol and a mock that answered from the packet. This is
   4: the real thing: the same :class:`~planbench_explanation.protocol.ToolSession`
   5: admission, evidence fetched from a declared source, checkers run, and
   6: results stamped with the card's refusals and the build that produced
   7: them.
   8: 
   9: **Three responsibilities, kept apart on purpose.**
  10: 
  11: *Admission* is the session's, and this module does not re-implement any
  12: of it. *Evidence* is an :class:`EvidenceSource`'s â€” a narrow protocol
  13: with one method per thing a tool needs, so a host can be pointed at a
  14: run directory, at a test fixture, or at nothing without any tool
  15: knowing. *Checking* is :mod:`planbench_explanation.checkers`', which are
  16: pure functions that never learn their request id or their card. The host
  17: is the only place the three meet, and it is the only place that may
  18: produce a :class:`~planbench_explanation.protocol.ToolResult`.
  19: 
  20: **Absence has a code, never a zero.** Every path where the evidence is
  21: not there returns ``not_checkable`` with a failure code from the card or
  22: from :data:`~planbench_explanation.protocol.HOST_FAILURE_CODES`. Two of
  23: the four mechanism checks are in that state permanently for now:
  24: ``replay_global_plan`` and ``rrt_convergence`` need planning inputs
  25: recorded as the run happened, which is the E4.5 sidecar and does not
  26: exist. They report ``checker_not_implemented``, which is the truth, and
  27: they will keep reporting it until there is something to replay from
  28: rather than something to reconstruct.
  29: 
  30: **The replay checker arrives as an argument, not as an import.** A
  31: replay needs a planner, and this package must not contain one â€” see
  32: :mod:`planbench_explanation.replay`. So a host is given a
  33: :class:`~planbench_explanation.replay.ReplayPlanner` or it is not, and
  34: without one ``replay_global_plan`` stays ``not_checkable`` exactly as it
  35: was. The dependency points from the simulator into here and never back.
  36: 
  37: **The evidence source is bound to the packet before anything runs.**
  38: A host given an :class:`AnalysisRequest` for one run and an evidence
  39: source pointed at another would admit every request correctly and then
  40: answer them from the wrong run's data, stamped ``recorded``. Nothing
  41: downstream could see it: the result names a tool and a request, not a
  42: run. So a source declares an :class:`EvidenceIdentity` and the
  43: constructor refuses a mismatch â€” before a checker exists to be wrong.
  44: 
  45: **A result's artifact reference points at a file that exists.** The
  46: first version composed a path and a checksum and wrote nothing there, so
  47: every completed result carried a reference an auditor could not resolve
  48: â€” a traceability field that traced to nothing, which is worse than an
  49: absent one because it looks like diligence. Writing goes through an
  50: :class:`EvidenceSink`, and the reference on the result is the one the
  51: sink returned after storing the bytes.
  52: 
  53: **The host signs with its own build, and that is a real limitation.**
  54: ``implementation_ref`` names the code that produced a result, and here
  55: it is whatever the caller declares the platform build to be. Within one
  56: process that is a statement of intent rather than proof; what actually
  57: binds a result to a run is the session's admitted request. The signature
  58: becomes load-bearing when results cross a process boundary, and this
  59: module is where that will need doing.

 162: class InMemoryEvidenceSink:
 163:     """Keeps artifacts in a dict. For tests and for a dry run.
 164: 
 165:     Not a null sink: a sink that discards would put the dangling
 166:     reference back, and the point of the protocol is that the reference
 167:     resolves to something. What it resolves to here is memory, and
 168:     :attr:`artifacts` is how a caller reads it.
 169: 
 170:     **Chosen explicitly, never defaulted to.** It was the host's default
 171:     sink, which meant a production host wrote every artifact into a dict
 172:     that dies with the process while its results kept a ``memory://``
 173:     reference that outlived it â€” a dangling pointer with a plausible
 174:     scheme. A host now requires a sink, and picking this one is a
 175:     statement that the results are not being kept.
 176:     """
 177: 
 178:     def __init__(self, prefix: str = "memory://explain") -> None:
 179:         self.prefix = prefix
 180:         self.artifacts: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
 181: 
 182:     def store(self, *, tool_id: str, request_id: str, payload: dict[str, object]) -> StoredEvidence:
 183:         ref = f"{self.prefix}/{tool_id}/{request_id}.json"
 184:         self.artifacts[ref] = payload
 185:         return StoredEvidence(artifact_ref=ref, checksum=artifact_checksum(payload))
 186: 
 187: 
 188: def _safe_name(value: str) -> str:
 189:     """A filename derived from an untrusted string.
 190: 
 191:     ``request_id`` comes from the analyst. The first version pasted it
 192:     into a path â€” ``../../outside`` would have written wherever it
 193:     pointed. The id is hashed rather than sanitised: a filter has to
 194:     anticipate every spelling of "go up a level", and a digest has
 195:     nothing to anticipate. The id itself is stored inside the artifact,
 196:     so a reader loses nothing.
 197:     """
 198:     return hashlib.sha256(value.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:32]

 201: class FileEvidenceSink:
 202:     """Writes artifacts under a root directory, one JSON file each.
 203: 
 204:     Two independent defences, because the first is a judgement about
 205:     strings and the second is a fact about paths: the filename comes
 206:     from a digest, and the resolved path is checked to be under the root
 207:     before anything is written.
 208:     """
 209: 
 210:     def __init__(self, root: Path, *, relative_to: Path | None = None) -> None:
 211:         self.root = root
 212:         self.relative_to = relative_to or root
 213: 
 214:     def store(self, *, tool_id: str, request_id: str, payload: dict[str, object]) -> StoredEvidence:
 215:         body = {"request_id": request_id, "tool_id": tool_id, **payload}
 216:         path = self.root / _safe_name(tool_id) / f"{_safe_name(request_id)}.json"
 217:         root = self.root.resolve()
 218:         if not path.resolve().is_relative_to(root):
 219:             raise EvidenceMismatch(
 220:                 f"refusing to write {path.resolve()} outside the artifact root {root}"
 221:             )
 222:         path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
 223:         path.write_text(
 224:             json.dumps(body, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")) + "\n", encoding="utf-8"
 225:         )
 226:         try:
 227:             ref = path.relative_to(self.relative_to).as_posix()
 228:         except ValueError:
 229:             ref = path.as_posix()
 230:         return StoredEvidence(artifact_ref=ref, checksum=artifact_checksum(body))

 307: class ReportEvidence:
 308:     """Evidence read off a scoring report and a measured map.
 309: 
 310:     Built **from the packet it will serve**, not told what it is about.
 311:     The report's own identity block and candidate rows are checked
 312:     against the packet at construction; the robot's radius, inflation
 313:     margin and required passage width are read off the packet rather
 314:     than accepted from the caller.
 315: 
 316:     The report is where the columns the latency check needs live, written
 317:     per episode at scoring time: ``peak_search_nodes``,
 318:     ``peak_tree_nodes`` and ``p99_latency_ms``.
 319: 
 320:     **The two node columns are not added together.** HÄ-6 separates a
 321:     grid search's expanded nodes from a sampling planner's tree size
 322:     because they count different things, and a candidate uses one or the
 323:     other. This picks whichever column the candidate's episodes actually
 324:     populate, and refuses when both are populated â€” a candidate reporting
 325:     both is one this reader does not understand, and guessing which
 326:     number is the search would be inventing the measurement.
 327: 
 328:     Latency is ``p99_latency_ms``, the pooled control-tick figure. Every
 329:     replan writes its own control-step row carrying the global planner's
 330:     latency (HÄ-6's ``replan_count`` note), so an episode with a large
 331:     search shows it there. It is a p99 over ticks rather than the
 332:     search's own wall time, which is one more reason the card's ceiling
 333:     is ``associated``.
 334: 
 335:     The map side takes an already-measured
 336:     :class:`~planbench_explanation.map_features.RouteFeatures` per
 337:     region rather than a grid, because measuring a route is E3's job and
 338:     doing it twice would be two answers to one question.
 339:     """
 340: 
 341:     def __init__(
 342:         self,
 343:         report: Mapping[str, object],
 344:         *,
 345:         packet: CasePacket,
 346:         regions: Mapping[tuple[str, str], RouteFeatures] = MappingProxyType({}),
 347:         sidecar_directory: Path | None = None,
 348:     ) -> None:
 349:         self.report = report
 350:         self.packet = packet
 351:         #: Where this run's ``<episode>.planning_inputs.jsonl`` files
 352:         #: live. Handed in rather than derived: the address is the
 353:         #: **trace layout's** rule (class, conditions fingerprint,
 354:         #: candidate), and re-deriving it here would put a second copy of
 355:         #: that rule in the layer least able to keep it current.
 356:         self.sidecar_directory = sidecar_directory
 357:         self._identity = identity_of(packet)
 358:         self.regions = regions
 359:         self._verify_report_is_about(packet)
 360: 
 361:     def _verify_report_is_about(self, packet: CasePacket) -> None:
 362:         """Check the report against the packet, rather than being told.
 363: 
 364:         The identity used to be a constructor argument beside the
 365:         report, so a caller could hand over run B's report and run A's
 366:         identity and pass the host's check â€” the binding stopped
 367:         accidental miswiring and was not a trust boundary. What can be
 368:         compared is compared here, from the report's own fields.
 369: 
 370:         What **cannot** be compared is named rather than skipped:
 371:         ``run_uri`` and ``run_checksum`` have no counterpart on the
 372:         packet, and neither does a map checksum, so those are recorded
 373:         below and not cross-checked. A reader should know which of these
 374:         the platform actually verified.
 375:         """
 376:         identity = self.report.get("identity")
 377:         if isinstance(identity, Mapping):
 378:             profile = identity.get("task_profile_id")
 379:             if profile is not None and profile != packet.task.task_profile_id:
 380:                 raise EvidenceMismatch(
 381:                     f"the report is about task profile {profile!r} and the packet "
 382:                     f"about {packet.task.task_profile_id!r}"
 383:                 )
 384:         reported = {
 385:             entry.get("candidate_id")
 386:             for entry in self.report.get("candidates", [])  # type: ignore[union-attr]
 387:             if isinstance(entry, Mapping)
 388:         }
 389:         if reported:
 390:             missing = sorted(
 391:                 candidate.candidate_id
 392:                 for candidate in packet.candidates
 393:                 if candidate.candidate_id not in reported
 394:             )
 395:             if missing:
 396:                 raise EvidenceMismatch(
 397:                     f"the report has no rows for {missing}, which the packet compares"
 398:                 )
 399: 
 400:     #: What the report says about itself that the packet cannot confirm.
 401:     #: Kept for an auditor and deliberately **not** treated as verified.
 402:     @property
 403:     def unverified_report_identity(self) -> dict[str, object]:
 404:         return {
 405:             "run_uri": self.report.get("run_uri"),
 406:             "run_checksum": self.report.get("run_checksum"),
 407:         }
 408: 
 409:     @property
 410:     def identity(self) -> EvidenceIdentity:
 411:         return self._identity
 412: 
 413:     def gap_evidence(self, *, candidate_id: str, region_id: str) -> GapEvidence | None:
 414:         """Robot facts come from the **packet**, never from the caller.
 415: 
 416:         They were constructor arguments, which meant the radius and the
 417:         margin a check compared against were whatever the caller said â€”
 418:         beside a packet that carries its own. Two sources for one fact
 419:         is one source too many, and the packet is the one the analyst
 420:         was shown.
 421:         """
 422:         features = self.regions.get((candidate_id, region_id))
 423:         if features is None:
 424:             return None
 425:         robot = self.packet.task.robot
 426:         if robot.inflation_margin_m is None or robot.required_passage_width_m is None:
 427:             # The run did not record the inflation. Absent rather than
 428:             # assumed â€” a clearance argument on a guessed margin is an
 429:             # argument about a costmap nobody configured.
 430:             return None
 431:         return GapEvidence(
 432:             region_id=region_id,
 433:             features=features,
 434:             robot_radius_m=robot.radius_m,
 435:             inflation_margin_m=robot.inflation_margin_m,
 436:             required_passage_width_m=robot.required_passage_width_m,
 437:         )
 438: 
 439:     def latency_evidence(self, *, candidate_id: str) -> LatencyEvidence | None:
 440:         rows = self._episode_rows(candidate_id)
 441:         column = self._node_column(rows)
 442:         if column is None:
 443:             return None
 444:         episodes = []
 445:         for row in rows:
 446:             nodes = row.get(column)
 447:             latency = row.get("p99_latency_ms")
 448:             context = row.get("episode_context_id")
 449:             if nodes is None or latency is None or not context:
 450:                 continue
 451:             episodes.append(
 452:                 EpisodeSearchCost(
 453:                     episode_context_id=str(context),
 454:                     expanded_nodes=int(nodes),
 455:                     planner_latency_ms=float(latency),
 456:                 )
 457:             )
 458:         if not episodes:
 459:             return None
 460:         return LatencyEvidence(candidate_id=candidate_id, episodes=tuple(episodes))
 461: 
 462:     @staticmethod
 463:     def _node_column(rows: Sequence[Mapping[str, object]]) -> str | None:
 464:         """Which of the two node columns this candidate populates.
 465: 
 466:         ``None`` when neither does â€” nothing to rank â€” and also when
 467:         both do, because a candidate reporting a grid frontier *and* a
 468:         sampling tree is one this reader has no rule for, and picking
 469:         one would be a guess presented as a measurement.
 470:         """
 471:         search = any(_positive(row.get("peak_search_nodes")) for row in rows)
 472:         tree = any(_positive(row.get("peak_tree_nodes")) for row in rows)
 473:         if search and tree:
 474:             return None
 475:         if search:
 476:             return "peak_search_nodes"
 477:         if tree:
 478:             return "peak_tree_nodes"
 479:         return None
 480: 
 481:     def _episode_rows(self, candidate_id: str) -> list[Mapping[str, object]]:
 482:         candidates = self.report.get("candidates")
 483:         if not isinstance(candidates, list):
 484:             return []
 485:         for entry in candidates:
 486:             if not isinstance(entry, Mapping) or entry.get("candidate_id") != candidate_id:
 487:                 continue
 488:             episodes = entry.get("episodes")
 489:             if isinstance(episodes, list):
 490:                 return [row for row in episodes if isinstance(row, Mapping)]
 491:         return []
 492: 
 493: 
 494: class ToolHost:
 495:     """Serves one analysis round against one evidence source."""
 496: 
 497:     def __init__(
 498:         self,
 499:         analysis: AnalysisRequest,
 500:         evidence: EvidenceSource,
 501:         *,
 502:         implementation_ref: str,
 503:         sink: EvidenceSink,
 504:         replay_planner: ReplayPlanner | None = None,
 505:         input_provenance: InputProvenance = "recorded",
 506:     ) -> None:
 507:         expected = identity_of(analysis.packet)
 508:         actual = evidence.identity
 509:         if actual != expected:
 510:             differing = sorted(
 511:                 field
 512:                 for field in expected.model_dump()
 513:                 if getattr(actual, field) != getattr(expected, field)
 514:             )
 515:             raise EvidenceMismatch(
 516:                 f"the evidence source is about a different run than the packet: "
 517:                 f"{differing} differ. Admission would have passed every request and "
 518:                 "answered it from the wrong run, stamped 'recorded', and nothing "
 519:                 "downstream names a run to notice with."
 520:             )
 521:         self.session = ToolSession(analysis)
 522:         self.analysis = analysis
 523:         self.evidence = evidence
 524:         self.implementation_ref = implementation_ref
 525:         self.sink = sink
 526:         self.replay_planner = replay_planner
 527:         self.input_provenance = input_provenance
 528: 
 529:     def call(self, request: ToolRequest) -> ToolResult:
 530:         """Admit, execute, record. Rejections propagate untouched.
 531: 
 532:         A rejection is not converted into a failed result: "the host
 533:         would not accept this request" and "the check ran and could not
 534:         answer" are different facts, and collapsing them would let an
 535:         analyst read a malformed request as evidence of absence.
 536:         """
 537:         card = self.session.admit(request)
 538:         result = self._execute(card, request)
 539:         self.session.record(result)
 540:         return result
 541: 
 542:     def _execute(self, card: ToolCard, request: ToolRequest) -> ToolResult:
 543:         if card.tool_id in AWAITING_SIDECAR:
 544:             return self._unavailable(card, request, "checker_not_implemented")
 545:         if card.tool_id == "gap_vs_footprint":
 546:             return self._gap(card, request)
 547:         if card.tool_id == "latency_vs_expanded_nodes":
 548:             return self._latency(card, request)
 549:         if card.tool_id == "replay_global_plan":
 550:             return self._replay(card, request)
 551:         if card.tool_id == "rrt_convergence":
 552:             return self._convergence(card, request)
 553:         return self._unavailable(card, request, "tool_unavailable")
 554: 
 555:     # -- the two checks this platform can run ----------------------------
 556: 
 557:     def _gap(self, card: ToolCard, request: ToolRequest) -> ToolResult:
 558:         evidence = self.evidence.gap_evidence(
 559:             candidate_id=str(request.arguments["candidate_id"]),
 560:             region_id=str(request.arguments["region_id"]),
 561:         )
 562:         if evidence is None:
 563:             return self._unavailable(card, request, "region_not_resolved")
 564:         try:
 565:             outcome = check_gap_vs_footprint(evidence)
 566:         except CheckerRefusal as error:
 567:             # The checker's own code, forwarded. It used to be inferred
 568:             # from the message, so improving a sentence relabelled the
 569:             # failure.
 570:             return self._unavailable(card, request, error.code)
 571:         return self._completed(
 572:             card,
 573:             request,
 574:             outcome,
 575:             references=(
 576:                 EvidenceReference(
 577:                     kind="map_region",
 578:                     ref=f"region:{evidence.region_id}",
 579:                     label="the passage the check measured",
 580:                 ),
 581:             ),
 582:         )
 583: 
 584:     def _latency(self, card: ToolCard, request: ToolRequest) -> ToolResult:
 585:         evidence = self.evidence.latency_evidence(
 586:             candidate_id=str(request.arguments["candidate_id"])
 587:         )
 588:         if evidence is None:
 589:             return self._unavailable(card, request, "expansion_counts_missing")
 590:         try:
 591:             outcome = check_latency_vs_expanded_nodes(evidence)
 592:         except CheckerRefusal as error:
 593:             return self._unavailable(card, request, error.code)
 594:         return self._completed(card, request, outcome)
 595: 
 596:     # -- shaping ---------------------------------------------------------
 597: 
 598:     def _completed(
 599:         self,
 600:         card: ToolCard,
 601:         request: ToolRequest,
 602:         outcome: CheckOutcome,
 603:         *,
 604:         references: tuple[EvidenceReference, ...] = (),
 605:     ) -> ToolResult:
 606:         stored = self.sink.store(
 607:             tool_id=card.tool_id,
 608:             request_id=request.request_id,
 609:             payload={
 610:                 "tool": list(card.key),
 611:                 "request": request.request_id,
 612:                 "run_id": self.analysis.packet.run_id,
 613:                 "arguments": dict(request.arguments),
 614:                 "proposition_type": outcome.proposition_type,
 615:                 "verdict": outcome.verdict,
 616:                 "measurements": outcome.measurements,
 617:                 "references": [reference.model_dump() for reference in references],
 618:                 "note": outcome.note,
 619:             },
 620:         )
 621:         return stamped_result(
 622:             card,
 623:             request,
 624:             execution_status="completed",
 625:             input_provenance=self.input_provenance,
 626:             proposition_verdict=outcome.verdict,
 627:             supported_propositions=(
 628:                 PropositionOutcome(
 629:                     proposition_id=f"{outcome.proposition_type}:{request.request_id}",
 630:                     proposition_type=outcome.proposition_type,
 631:                     result=outcome.verdict,
 632:                 ),
 633:             ),
 634:             measurements=outcome.measurements,
 635:             references=references,
 636:             evidence_artifact_ref=stored.artifact_ref,
 637:             evidence_checksum=stored.checksum,
 638:             implementation_ref=self.implementation_ref,
 639:         )
 640: 
 641:     def _replay(self, card: ToolCard, request: ToolRequest) -> ToolResult:
 642:         if self.replay_planner is None:
 643:             # No planner was injected. Not a failure of the run: this
 644:             # host was built without the half that can re-run a query.
 645:             return self._unavailable(card, request, "checker_not_implemented")
 646:         evidence = self.evidence.replay_evidence(
 647:             candidate_id=str(request.arguments["candidate_id"]),
 648:             episode_context_id=str(request.arguments["episode_context_id"]),
 649:             planning_attempt=int(request.arguments["attempt_index"]),
 650:         )
 651:         if evidence is None:
 652:             return self._unavailable(card, request, "planning_inputs_missing")
 653:         try:
 654:             outcome = check_replay_global_plan(evidence, planner=self.replay_planner)
 655:         except CheckerRefusal as error:
 656:             return self._unavailable(card, request, error.code)
 657:         except ReplayUnavailable as error:
 658:             # The harness said it cannot rebuild this planner. A harness
 659:             # that cannot run has refuted nothing.
 660:             return self._unavailable(card, request, str(error.code))
 661:         return self._completed(card, request, outcome)
 662: 
 663:     def _convergence(self, card: ToolCard, request: ToolRequest) -> ToolResult:
 664:         if self.replay_planner is None:
 665:             return self._unavailable(card, request, "checker_not_implemented")
 666:         evidence = self.evidence.convergence_evidence(
 667:             candidate_id=str(request.arguments["candidate_id"]),
 668:             episode_context_id=str(request.arguments["episode_context_id"]),
 669:             planning_attempt=1,
 670:         )
 671:         if evidence is None:
 672:             return self._unavailable(card, request, "planning_inputs_missing")
 673:         try:
 674:             outcome = check_rrt_convergence(evidence, planner=self.replay_planner)
 675:         except CheckerRefusal as error:
 676:             return self._unavailable(card, request, error.code)
 677:         except ReplayUnavailable as error:
 678:             return self._unavailable(card, request, str(error.code))
 679:         return self._completed(card, request, outcome)
 680: 
 681:     def _unavailable(self, card: ToolCard, request: ToolRequest, code: str) -> ToolResult:
 682:         return stamped_result(
 683:             card,
 684:             request,
 685:             execution_status="not_checkable",
 686:             input_provenance="missing",
 687:             failure_code=code,
 688:         )
 689: 
 690: 
 691: def _positive(value: object) -> bool:
 692:     """A node count that says something happened."""
 693:     return isinstance(value, (int, float)) and not isinstance(value, bool) and value > 0
 694: 
 695:     def replay_evidence(
 696:         self, *, candidate_id: str, episode_context_id: str, planning_attempt: int
 697:     ) -> ReplayEvidence | None:
 698:         """One recorded attempt and the snapshot it pins, or ``None``.
 699: 
 700:         ``None`` where the run predates the sidecar or the attempt was
 701:         never recorded â€” the host turns that into ``not_checkable``,
 702:         which is the truthful answer and the one the evidence ladder
 703:         already prices.
 704:         """
 705:         if self.sidecar_directory is None:
 706:             return None
 707:         path = self.sidecar_directory / f"{episode_context_id}.planning_inputs.jsonl"
 708:         if not path.exists():
 709:             return None
 710:         header, records = read_sidecar(path)
 711:         if header.candidate_id != candidate_id:
 712:             raise EvidenceMismatch(
 713:                 f"the sidecar at {path} is {header.candidate_id!r}'s and the request "
 714:                 f"is about {candidate_id!r}"
 715:             )
 716:         for record in records:
 717:             if record.planning_attempt == planning_attempt:
 718:                 return ReplayEvidence(
 719:                     record=record,
 720:                     snapshot=snapshot_for(path, record),
 721:                     inputs_loaded_from_record=True,
 722:                 )
 723:         return None
 724: 
 725:     def convergence_evidence(
 726:         self, *, candidate_id: str, episode_context_id: str, planning_attempt: int
 727:     ) -> ConvergenceEvidence | None:
 728:         """One recorded query, plus the seeds this candidate actually ran.
 729: 
 730:         **The seed set comes from the run's own sidecars**, one per
 731:         episode, not from the report and not from the caller. The report
 732:         does not carry seeds â€” its episodes are context hashes â€” and a
 733:         caller-supplied set would be the same self-declared value the
 734:         evidence identity already had to stop being. What the run drew
 735:         from is recorded in the runs it made.
 736: 
 737:         Sampling planners only: an episode whose snapshot records no
 738:         seed contributes none, and a candidate that never records one
 739:         yields no evidence rather than a sweep over a seed set of
 740:         ``[0]``.
 741:         """
 742:         replay = self.replay_evidence(
 743:             candidate_id=candidate_id,
 744:             episode_context_id=episode_context_id,
 745:             planning_attempt=planning_attempt,
 746:         )
 747:         if replay is None or self.sidecar_directory is None:
 748:             return None
 749: 
 750:         seeds: list[int] = []
 751:         for path in sorted(self.sidecar_directory.glob("*.planning_inputs.jsonl")):
 752:             header, records = read_sidecar(path)
 753:             if header.candidate_id != candidate_id or not records:
 754:                 continue
 755:             seed = snapshot_for(path, records[0]).seed
 756:             if seed is not None and seed not in seeds:
 757:                 seeds.append(seed)
 758:         if not seeds:
 759:             return None
 760:         return ConvergenceEvidence(
 761:             record=replay.record, snapshot=replay.snapshot, seeds=tuple(seeds)
 762:         )

1: """Provider selection across vendors.
   2: 
   3: One rule: a missing API key degrades the agent, it never breaks the
   4: platform. With nothing configured the deterministic mock takes over, the
   5: whole M8 surface stays available, and every response records which
   6: provider produced it â€” so nobody mistakes a keyword-matched answer for a
   7: model-written one.
   8: 
   9: Selecting a provider explicitly that is not usable raises instead of
  10: silently downgrading. An explicit choice should fail loudly; only
  11: ``auto`` is allowed to fall back.
  12: """
  13: 
  14: from __future__ import annotations
  15: 
  16: import importlib.util
  17: import logging
  18: import os
  19: from dataclasses import dataclass
  20: 
  21: from planbench_agent.openai_provider import PRESETS, OpenAICompatibleProvider
  22: from planbench_agent.provider import LLMProvider, MockProvider, ProviderUnavailable
  23: 
  24: logger = logging.getLogger("planbench.agent.factory")
  25: 
  26: MOCK = "mock"
  27: ANTHROPIC = "anthropic"
  28: AUTO = "auto"
  29: 
  30: #: Every provider that can be named in ``PLANBENCH_AGENT_PROVIDER``.
  31: PROVIDERS: tuple[str, ...] = (AUTO, MOCK, ANTHROPIC, *sorted(PRESETS))
  32: 
  33: #: Order ``auto`` tries. Anthropic first because its adapter is the one
  34: #: written against first-party documentation; the rest follow the shared
  35: #: OpenAI-compatible wire format. ``local`` is last and only picked when
  36: #: named explicitly â€” an unreachable localhost port should not silently
  37: #: become the configured provider.
  38: AUTO_ORDER: tuple[str, ...] = (
  39:     ANTHROPIC,
  40:     "openai",
  41:     "gemini",
  42:     "openrouter",
  43:     "groq",
  44:     "deepseek",
  45:     "xai",
  46: )
  47: 
  48: 
  49: @dataclass(frozen=True)
  50: class ProviderStatus:
  51:     """Whether one provider is ready, and what is missing if not."""
  52: 
  53:     name: str
  54:     api_key_env: str
  55:     key_present: bool
  56:     sdk_installed: bool
  57:     sdk_package: str
  58: 
  59:     @property
  60:     def ready(self) -> bool:
  61:         return self.key_present and self.sdk_installed
  62: 
  63:     @property
  64:     def missing(self) -> str:
  65:         if self.ready:
  66:             return ""
  67:         gaps = []
  68:         if not self.key_present and self.api_key_env:
  69:             gaps.append(f"set {self.api_key_env}")
  70:         if not self.sdk_installed:
  71:             gaps.append(f"pip install {self.sdk_package}")
  72:         return "; ".join(gaps)
  73: 
  74: 
  75: def _anthropic_key_env() -> str:
  76:     from planbench_agent.anthropic_provider import API_KEY_ENV
  77: 
  78:     return API_KEY_ENV
  79: 
  80: 
  81: def provider_status() -> tuple[ProviderStatus, ...]:
  82:     """Readiness of every configurable provider, for diagnostics.
  83: 
  84:     Surfaced through ``GET /agent/capabilities`` so "why is it still
  85:     using the mock?" is answerable without reading the logs.
  86:     """
  87:     key_env = _anthropic_key_env()
  88:     statuses = [
  89:         ProviderStatus(
  90:             name=ANTHROPIC,
  91:             api_key_env=key_env,
  92:             key_present=bool(os.environ.get(key_env)),
  93:             sdk_installed=_can_import("anthropic"),
  94:             sdk_package="anthropic",
  95:         )
  96:     ]
  97:     for kind in sorted(PRESETS):
  98:         preset = PRESETS[kind]
  99:         statuses.append(
 100:             ProviderStatus(
 101:                 name=kind,
 102:                 api_key_env=preset.api_key_env,
 103:                 key_present=(not preset.requires_key) or bool(os.environ.get(preset.api_key_env)),
 104:                 sdk_installed=_can_import("openai"),
 105:                 sdk_package="openai",
 106:             )
 107:         )
 108:     return tuple(statuses)
 109: 
 110: 
 111: def _can_import(module: str) -> bool:
 112:     return importlib.util.find_spec(module) is not None
 113: 
 114: 
 115: def build_provider(
 116:     kind: str = AUTO,
 117:     *,
 118:     model: str | None = None,
 119:     api_key: str | None = None,
 120:     base_url: str | None = None,
 121: ) -> LLMProvider:
 122:     """Return a provider for ``kind``.
 123: 
 124:     ``model`` is required for the OpenAI-compatible providers: model ids
 125:     there change often enough that a hardcoded default would eventually
 126:     404, and guessing one is worse than asking. The Anthropic adapter
 127:     carries its own documented default.
 128:     """
 129:     kind = (kind or AUTO).strip().lower()
 130:     if kind not in PROVIDERS:
 131:         raise ValueError(f"unknown provider {kind!r}; expected one of {PROVIDERS}")
 132: 
 133:     if kind == MOCK:
 134:         return MockProvider()
 135:     if kind == AUTO:
 136:         return _auto(model=model, api_key=api_key, base_url=base_url)
 137:     return _named(kind, model=model, api_key=api_key, base_url=base_url)
 138: 
 139: 
 140: def _named(
 141:     kind: str, *, model: str | None, api_key: str | None, base_url: str | None
 142: ) -> LLMProvider:
 143:     if kind == ANTHROPIC:
 144:         from planbench_agent.anthropic_provider import DEFAULT_MODEL, AnthropicProvider
 145: 
 146:         return AnthropicProvider(model=model or DEFAULT_MODEL, api_key=api_key)
 147:     return OpenAICompatibleProvider.for_provider(
 148:         kind, model_id=model or "", api_key=api_key, base_url=base_url
 149:     )
 150: 
 151: 
 152: def _auto(*, model: str | None, api_key: str | None, base_url: str | None) -> LLMProvider:
 153:     for kind in AUTO_ORDER:
 154:         if not _auto_ready(kind):
 155:             continue
 156:         if kind != ANTHROPIC and not model:
 157:             # A key alone is not enough for these: without a model id the
 158:             # first request would fail. Say so and keep looking.
 159:             logger.warning("provider %r has a key but no PLANBENCH_AGENT_MODEL; skipping it", kind)
 160:             continue
 161:         provider = _named(kind, model=model, api_key=api_key, base_url=base_url)
 162:         logger.info("agent provider: %s (%s)", provider.name, provider.model)
 163:         return provider
 164: 
 165:     logger.info(
 166:         "agent provider: deterministic mock (no provider key found); answers are "
 167:         "keyword-matched, not model-generated. Configure one with "
 168:         "PLANBENCH_AGENT_PROVIDER + the matching API key."
 169:     )
 170:     return MockProvider()
 171: 
 172: 
 173: def _auto_ready(kind: str) -> bool:
 174:     if kind == ANTHROPIC:
 175:         from planbench_agent.anthropic_provider import AnthropicProvider
 176: 
 177:         return AnthropicProvider.available()
 178:     return OpenAICompatibleProvider.available(kind)
 179: 
 180: 
 181: def describe_unavailable(kind: str) -> str:
 182:     """Human-readable reason a named provider cannot be used, or ''."""
 183:     for status in provider_status():
 184:         if status.name == kind:
 185:             return status.missing
 186:     return f"unknown provider {kind!r}"
 187: 
 188: 
 189: def require_provider(kind: str, *, model: str | None = None) -> LLMProvider:
 190:     """Build a named provider, raising with the fix if it is not ready."""
 191:     reason = describe_unavailable(kind)
 192:     if reason:
 193:         raise ProviderUnavailable(f"provider {kind!r} is not usable: {reason}")
 194:     return build_provider(kind, model=model)
 195: 
 196: 
 197: __all__ = [
 198:     "ANTHROPIC",
 199:     "AUTO",
 200:     "AUTO_ORDER",
 201:     "MOCK",
 202:     "PROVIDERS",
 203:     "ProviderStatus",
 204:     "build_provider",
 205:     "describe_unavailable",
 206:     "provider_status",
 207:     "require_provider",
 208: ]

   2: 
   3: Nothing below names a vendor. Domain code (mission parsing, tool
   4: calling, report writing) depends only on :class:`LLMProvider`, so the
   5: backing model can be swapped â€” or replaced by the deterministic mock â€”
   6: without touching a single line of agent logic.

  11:   capability later (say, a cache hint) means one optional field, not a
  12:   signature change in every provider.
